PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - DORM ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: YOUNG NED sits Indian-style on the floor, shooting marbles by
his lonesome. Behind him, two LARGE GLASS TERRARIUMS house a
SNAKE and a RABBIT.
When it came to the currency of popularity,
Young Ned was poor... but not the poorest.
The door swings open and EUGENE MULCHANDANI, headgear and all,
scuttles in.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Eugene Mulchandani’s thick accent and
unfortunate family history of disproportionate
jaw structure made him both extremely difficult
to understand and an easy mark for bullies.
Eugene plops down beside Ned, who offers him a shooter.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Young Ned knew that playing with Eugene meant
losing his marbles, but he considered the
sacrificed aggies, steelies and shooters a
donation to a good cause. For aside from Ned,
Eugene had only 2 other companions at the
Longborough School.
ON THE TWO TERRARIUMS
One looks like a swath of jungle and houses the snake, while the
rabbit’s home looks like a farmer’s garden.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Bilbo, his lethargic Indian Python, and Ackbar,
a bunny suffering from a condition similar to
Attention Deficit, Hyperactivity Disorder.
Ackbar, the rabbit, bounces anxiously in its cage.
BACK ON the boys and their marbles. Eugene’s attempt to shoot a
marble backfires, and we TRACK the MARBLE as it sails across the
room and--
--SMASHES against the glass of Bilbo’s cage and ricochets into
the glass of Ackbar’s, SHATTERING them both. A stare down
between the animals lasts but a moment before Snake slithers
toward Rabbit.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Eugene and Ned SCREAM as they watch helplessly. Eugene’s scream
cuts short when his eyes roll back and he faints!
OMIT
Young Ned carries a shoebox and drags a large burlap sack into a
clearing.
Eugene was devastated when he learned that,
upon attempting to eat Ackbar the Bunny,
Bilbo the Snake choked, killing them both.
Young Ned kneels, opening the shoebox to REVEAL a very-dead
Ackbar the Bunny.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Under the guise of burying Eugene’s pets,
Young Ned resolved to perform another act of
charity for his language-mangling friend.
Ned touches Ackbar, bringing him back to life. He places the
lid carefully back over the rambunctious bunny.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He knew that giving Eugene his friends back
would require 2 innocent creatures to die...
A SQUIRREL drops from a tree in front of Ned. Ned opens the
burlap sack and grimaces a moment at Bilbo.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and a lie about how he found them both
barely breathing when he went to bury them.
Ned darts his finger into the bag and quickly jerks it out,
falling on his keister as he quickly pulls the now-squirming bag
shut again.

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL - DORM ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Eugene, upon seeing Bilbo back in his cage, Ackbar in his, pulls
Ned into a slobbery hug.
But as long as the benefits outweighed the
costs, he also believed an act of charity
outweighed the consequences.
Establishing...
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
Several pie tins host empty crusts. Into one plunks some
delicious strawberry filling.
20 years, 16 weeks, 4 days and 9 hours later,
the boy had grown into the Pie-Maker, and the
Pie-Maker was at this very moment... troubled.
NED, all grown-up, gently covers the strawberry pie with dough
for a crust. CHUCK pokes her head through the door, seeing that
pies cover every inch of surface space.
You’re stress baking.
Ned looks up, brow unfurrowing at the sight of Chuck.
I don’t know what you’re talking about.
I’m talking about you’ve been up since before
the sun and there’s a traffic jam of pies
waiting to exit into the oven. You’re worried
about something.
“Worried” would imply an urge to action.
“Troubled” seems more apt.
About a mysterious man named Dwight who came
asking questions about your dad and is now
dating my Aunt Vivian?
OLIVE enters, stopping short at the plethora of pies.
You’re stress baking.
If he’s dating your aunt, he’s going to see a
picture of you, and unless he has retrograde
amnesia, he’s going to recognize you. Or
already has.
PLUNK-PLUNK! Two more pies filled up as Ned’s stress level
rises.
NED (CONT’D)
Why is he dating your aunt? Not to suggest that
she’s not datable and perfectly lovely, but it
does seem more than a little coincidental.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
(an epiphany)
Does Vivian’s nice-smelling new boy toy have
something to do with why you faked your death?
NED / CHUCK
No.
(to Chuck)
Because maybe he’s been after you all along.
Maybe he works for the IRS. If anybody’s
going to figure out you’re not really dead,
it’s the Tax Man. Or maybe he thinks you
really are dead and he’s one of those
paranormal investigators. Maybe he’s the old
priest and a young priest is coming.
That would be a waste of religion. Because
she’s not.
(off their looks)
Dead.
Ned slops some pie filling on the floor as he overloads.
NED (CONT’D)
I find myself being urged to action.
Me, too.
Public records. Criminal records. We need to
find out who Dwight is and if he’s after more
than just your aunt’s companionship.
(to Olive)
Do you mind finding out what he’s told my mom
and aunt? Maybe plant a bug in their ears
that he has a penchant for untruths.
That way, if he realizes you’re alive and rats
you out, maybe they won’t believe it...
Olive scoops up a nearby pie box.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Counter-intelligence via pie delivery. Like
gossiping with a purpose. My speciality.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
The front door swings open to REVEAL Olive, pie box in hand.
Pie time!
REVERSE TO REVEAL VIVIAN, all smiles at the sight of Olive.
Olive! What a surprise! And with a pie...
The second sweetest treat of my day.
Something sweeter than a Pie Hole pie?
Olive enters, where she sees DWIGHT and LILY sitting in the
living room.
The first was a surprise visit from a certain
gentleman caller.
The young lady of the Hole. And with a
special delivery to heel.
He stands to greet her as he speaks.
No need to stand on my account. Just here
doing my duty. No other reason that I can
speak of. What type of duty are you in again?
Clergy? Tax services?
Dwight collects and appraises antiques.
Which I learned right after he told me he’s
dating my sister.
Lily’s naturally suspicious of new liaisons,
but I felt compelled to come clean about our
relationship. Sneaking around is for
politicians in bathroom stalls.
Not for a brisk and bucolic autumn-cum-winter
afternoon on the park.
(tipping his hat)
Ladies.
He escorts Vivian to the door, following her out.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
He seems nice.
I don’t trust him further than I can spit.
And I can spit.
Lily pulls the curtain back from the window and peers.
LILY (CONT’D)
Ugh. Look at the way he drapes himself all
over her. Makes me want to stick a fork in my
eye. I need a drink.
She starts for the kitchen.
You’re holding one.
I need a stronger one. And a fork.
Lily disappears into the kitchen.
While Olive pondered one sister blinded by
love and the other by distrust...
...Emerson Cod pondered the exorbitant amount
of cash he’d just been offered.
EMERSON sits across from DANIEL HILL, ESQ., 40ish, well-polished
and cucumber cool and a very LOUD TALKER.
I demand justice for the decedent and will
not rest, settle or adjourn until I have it.
He pounds his fist on the table for impact.
Mind demanding it in your inside voice?
Sorry. Years of litigation have made me a
loud talker.
Why’s a dead man’s lawyer so willing to shell
out his own green over a client’s death?
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
I have a special practice. Gustav was my one
client and that client is now dead.
Ever hear about the difference between a
lawyer and a leech?
When you die, a leech will stop sucking your
blood and drop off.
He dead now. Why you still hangin’ on?
Lookin’ for a few stray cash capillaries?
Gustav was more than a client. He was a
cantankerous bombast with a violent temper
and a lust for power and wealth. In lawyer
speak, he was a friend.
Go to the police about your friend?
The police station is run by a bunch of
monkeys. You want the best, pay a premium.
And why ain’t the family paying the premium?
His family was his wife, and she was the
biggest leech of all. Always after his will.
You think she found a way to his will through
murder.
I never trusted her and tried my best, as a
lawyer and a friend, to protect Gustav. She
ruined his life. She's going to ruin his
legacy. But if I can prove she killed him, I
can annul that will and send her to the big
house where she belongs.
I smell a big ol’ “but” heading my direction.
Gustav was robbed the night he died. It
happens, when you have a fortune like his.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED: (2)
What kind of fortune we talkin’ ‘bout?
The kind built upon your tight balls.
Off Emerson’s sidelong glance, Daniel nods to the row of YARN
BALLS behind him. In the corner, an automatic yarn-baller
WHIRS, quietly spinning a skein of yarn into a ball.
The facts were these:

scenes.heading: INT. INFOMERCIAL STUDIO - 1950 - DAY - FLASHBACK (BLACK & WHITE)

lines.text: An ELDERLY WOMAN sits in an easy chair in front of a pleated
curtain, slowly winding a ball of yarn. The ball comes undone,
and the old woman shakes her head at the tangled mess.
The son of Eastern European potato farmers,
Gustav Hofer had lived the American dream.
WIDEN to REVEAL SMILING, YOUNG GUSTAV (19), holding a large YARN-
SWIFT, feeding yarn to the ELECTRIC BALL-WINDER behind him.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His mechanized yarn-baller not only gave a
generation of frustrated grandmothers the
means to make unwanted gifts...
Young Gustav hands the spun yarn ball to the grateful old lady.
And the words, “IN STORES NOW!” flash on screen...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...at the age of 19, it made Gustav Hofer his
first of countless millions.
As Gustav continues to mug for the camera, his face MORPHS into:

scenes.heading: INT. GUSTAV’S MANSION - RECENT PAST - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: GUSTAV HOFER, gray-haired and 80.
Unfortunately, his wealth attracted bad stock,
from gold-digging wives to desperate robbers.
Gustav’s head snaps skyward as--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Before Gustav Hofer could make one penny more,
someone arranged for his permanent retirement.
--a giant crystal chandelier CRASHES down, crushing Gustav!
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
Emerson, Ned and Chuck stand over the body of the late Gustav
Hofer, still ensconced within his chandelier.
He doesn’t look like the richest man in town.
They say he had the Midas touch. You ever
stop to consider that you’re a lot like King
Midas? Except substitute “life” for “gold.”
And you don’t have donkey ears.
Midas was a miser. Like Scrooge, but
hungrier. I’m a philanthropist.
Magic-fingered philanthropists wake dead
people and find out who killed ‘em. You wake
dead people, find out who killed ‘em and take
a third of my cut.
Non-profits still incur costs. Without your
donations, the Pie Hole would sink.
Touch the sucker.
Ned reaches down and ZAP! The chandelier lights briefly FLICKER
ON with the familiar POP of electricity, then go dark as
Gustav’s eyes snap open--
Hi, Mr. Hofer. We’d like to ask you a few
questions, but we’ve only got one minute.
I presume I’m dead.
Chuck starts to respond. Before she can:
GUSTAV HOFER (CONT’D)
Let’s get down to business. First, the matter
of my will.
It’s in your lawyer’s possessio--
Not that will. And don’t interrupt me, bucko.
I have a new will. And you’re going to track
it down for me, roger?
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED:
Roger. Now if you could--
I like you, kid, but you talk too much. The
will is in my trophy room. Go to the biggest
trophy -- center of the wall. Turn it
counterclockwise. Say it back to me.
Who killed you?
Who are you? Who is he? Do you know who I
am, Elmer?
You about to be the first man ever to be
murdered twice. You want justice or--
I don’t want my hard-earned money going where
it doesn’t belong. Your generation has never
understood the value of a dollar. I started
working when I was 8 years old and I didn’t--
Trophy room, big trophy, rotate counterclockwise.
Smartest one of the bunch. I like your moxie,
sass-o-fras. Find my will and make sure that
no-good, gold-digging wife of mine doesn’t get
one damn dime. Got it?
Who killed you?
The bellman did it. After I refused to pay
him. Who expects money for nothing?
ZAP! Ned re-deads the hard-nosed businessman. The POP of
electricity shorts the chandelier again, this time sending
lightbulbs POPPING in a FLURRY OF SPARKS. They all duck.
As they peek their heads back over the table, we...
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 11.
Emerson, Ned and Chuck are led by a BUTLER through the
ostentatious hall.
Assuming the bellman with an axe to grind was
Gustav’s longtime porter, and hoping that his new
will might hold some indication of motive,
Emerson Cod decided to kill 2 birds with 1 stone.
Dead Girl ‘n’ me will chat up the bellman
while you track down the trophy room and find
the will.
I can do that.
I always know when you about to move from
talking plans to talking personal by the way
you get so helpy.
I resent that. I’m helpy by nature.
(can’t help himself)
That being said, what’s your take on Dwight
dating Vivian? How long before he sees
Chuck’s picture and says, “Hey, look, that
waitress from the Pie Hole.”
When I see an out-of-context picture of a nice-
looking young girl, I don’t think, “Hey, look,
that nice-looking young girl who made my
cappuccino at that one restaurant.”
(then, noticing the wallpaper)
This wallpaper’s vintage Osborne & Little. You
could buy a small island for how much it cost.
Chuck turns around, almost crashing into ELISE HOFER, 24,
Gustav’s Anna Nicole-type widow, as she enters.
Cool. I never even noticed. Isn’t that
awful? I’m, like, the worst widow ever.
(extending a dainty hand)
Elise. You must be the P.I.s.
We are... thanks for agreeing to help us. You
must be devastated.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 12.
CONTINUED:
Crushed. Please, pop a squat... James-
Andrew, that’s the bellman you want to see, is
on his way. I told him to bring some of those
awesome champagne-juice drinks he makes.
Mimosas?
Sure. Whatever.
(yelling)
James-Andrew! They want mimosas instead!
JAMES-ANDREW! I’m sure he heard me.
You have a beautiful... castle, Mrs. Hofer.
Thanks... it’s a wreck now, getting it all set
up for the wake.
(then)
You should totally come. Everybody who’s
anybody is going to be here celebrating
Gustav’s death.
You mean “life.”
Same diff.
Is there a restroom?
Down the hall, second left.
Ned excuses himself.
The door swings open and Ned slides in and stops cold.
Oh, no.
REVERSE SHOT TO REVEAL a game-hunting room -- the “trophies” are
the stuffed animal heads that cover the wall and a PRIDE of
STUFFED LIONS in the center of the room.
Ned stares at the giant LION poised on a rock in the center of
all the other beasts.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 13.
CONTINUED:
NED (CONT’D)
“Turn the biggest trophy counterclockwise.”
Great.
JAMES-ANDREW, 29, Gustav’s put-upon bellman, serves the mimosas.
Best champagne-juice drink I’ve ever had.
I know, right?
Mrs. Hofer said you wanted to see me. I
assume it’s not just for my mimosa.
How does someone become a bellman, anyway?
James-Andrew takes umbrage.
Bellmen wear monkey-suits and work in hotel
lobbies. I am a porter.
What were you porting the night your boss had
a close encounter with his light fixture?
Nothing. I was at a key party. At least 15
people can vouch.
James-Andrew is definitely not the killing type.
Mrs. Hofer, forgive me for being blunt, but
you stand to gain the most from your late
husband’s death.
Elise GASPS, clutching her chest with exaggerated drama.
Oh, my god. You think I totally did it?
Well, FYI, I was at a charity ball the night
of the murder.
They’re all caught off-guard by the echo of a LION’S ROAR.
Was that a bear?
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.

scenes.heading: INT. GUSTAV’S MANSION - TROPHY ROOM - DAY

lines.text: Ned rotates the pedestal that holds the (already dead-again)
lion, which CLICKS open a metal door flush against the wall.
Taking extreme care not to brush against any of the other angry-
looking animals, Ned pulls the door open, finding the safe
EMPTY. Hastily-scrawled inside is the handwritten phrase:
“ORBIS PRO VOX.”
Ned rejoins Chuck and Emerson, who are waiting for him.
The safe was empty. No will. Nothing but a
cryptic Latin phrase.
Poor Gustav... all he cared about was getting
that will into the right hands.
We find the killer, we gonna find the will.
Bad news is our case just went from slam dunk
to buh-dunk-uh-dunk.
Is “buh-dunk-uh-dunk” bad?
Buh-dunk-uh-dunk means “big,” as in that’s
what our simple, little murder just became.
What happened to “the bellman did it”?
He’s hiding something, but 15 strangers
vouching is an airtight alibi.
What is a “key party,” anyway?
I love that you don’t know that. It’s like...
a raffle.
Of the porno variety.
Oh. Oh. Back to the case. How does a safe
with some cryptic Latin phrase scrawled inside
change anything?
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED:
You need to peel back the pie crust you working
under and try turning on the news. Rich folks
in this town are getting robbed right and left
by some happy hooligan who leaves the same
Latin calling card at every scene.
So that’s why this is a “buh-dunk-uh-dunk.”
If we dealing with a serial robber, there’s
gonna be more police attention than usual.
(then)
I got to go see a friend at the police station.
Great. Gives us an opportunity to start our
research project on Dwight.
Ned, Chuck and Olive sit before a stack of papers, files, phone
books and so on.
It’s like the mysterious Dwight didn’t exist
before checking into the Come-and-Sleep Motel.
Who knows... maybe he’s not such a bad guy.
He’s very charming. And he still smells nice.
What do Lily and Vivian think about him?
What you’d expect. Lily hates and Vivian is
completely ga.
(to Chuck)
Good news is you’re not on his radar.
Olive heads off. Ned and Chuck stare at their glut of paperwork.
We know Dwight’s got a strange preoccupation
with your father’s pocket watch. Maybe we
give it to him and he goes away.
Or we could wake my dad and ask him.
Chuck--
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
I’m just saying, it could be a big shortcut to
figuring out who Dwight is and what he wants
if we just woke my dad and asked him.
I’m sorry... it’s just, I know you want to say
goodbye to your father, and I know that a
lifetime of goodbyes can’t be condensed into a
single minute. Even if they could, you’d have
to watch him die all over again, and I love
you too much to make you suffer like that.
Chuck absorbs it all.
NED (CONT’D)
You understand? I hope?
She half-smiles, understanding but not liking it. Before she
can say anything, Emerson enters and joins them.
I got us a good nugget. Police say our serial
robber always makes a donation to charity day
after he robs someone.
(then)
Am I interrupting something?
No. Yes.
How’d you get them to tell you?
They didn’t know about the inscription in
Hofer’s secret safe, so we traded information.
Sounds like Gustav Hofer was robbed by a
latter-day Robin Hood.
And killed by him.
Call him whatever you want. I know where we
gonna find a bellman with a charity streak.
The Mod Squad stands in the midst of DOZENS AND DOZENS OF PEOPLE
milling about in old-time bellhop uniforms, chatting casually.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
Somewhere, a hand bell TING-A-LINGS and the group falls silent.
ROB WRIGHT, 35, confident, friendly and head of the Bellmen,
leaps onto the main counter.
It’s a new day, friends! Another opportunity
to help the needy. Ring your bells, collect
spare change and remember: Ring for Right!
The congregation replies in cheery unison:
Ring for Right!
The Bellmen produce their own bells and start RINGING furiously
before picking up their large, red donation kettles and
dispersing.
“Ring for Right.” Orbis Pro Vox.
Which means “yo’ ass is busted” in P.I. lingo.
Rob spots the strangers in his midst and heads over.
Welcome to the Bellmen Charities Headquarters.
Are you here to make a donation? Volunteer?
One of your bell-ringers rang for wrong. To
the tune of robbery-homicide.
I beg your pardon, but that’s outrageous. And
impossible. We screen our Bellmen regularly
to make sure all who ring in these hallowed
halls follow our motto: Ring for Right!
Which just happens to be written at crime scenes
all over the city. In a dead language, but still.
Friends, I assure you the Bellmen have nothing
to hide. I fling my doors open to your
investigation. And if there’s anything I can
do, don’t hesitate--
“To ring”?
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED: (2)
I was going to say “call.” But if clever was
a contest, you would win.
Rob heads off. Ned’s eyes are locked on their first target.
I know where we should start...
He nods to the far wall. Several PHONE OPERATORS sit in small
booths, aggressively speaking into their phones.
NED (CONT’D)
Telemarketers. I hate these guys.
The Mod Squad approaches the first booth, housing the most
vehement of the group -- TAM FONG, 27, clearly misguided as he
wears the uniform for the power and the chicks.
(into the phone)
Somewhere, a starving street child is chewing
off his own fingers ‘cause you’re too cheap to
give fifty bucks!
He slams down the phone, surprised when he looks up to find the
Mod Squad. He quickly stashes his call list in a folder.
Emerson Cod, P.I. These are my associates.
Care if we take a gander at your phone list?
What phone list?
The one you just slid into that folder.
What folder?
He moves the folder to a drawer beneath his desk and locks it.
There’s a comfort to knowing telemarketers are
as horrible in real life.
Shift change!
He puts a “Next Booth” sign on his desk and scurries away.
He was very suspect-ish.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED: (3)
Very.
Emerson grabs a paperclip off Tam’s desk and picks the drawer’s
lock lickety-split. He grabs the folder with Tam’s phone list
out before anyone glances his way.
Any of these phone numbers match up to Gustav’s
mansion, his ass gonna be very jailbird-ish.
The sound of a BENNY GOODMAN-esque CLARINET LOVE SONG carries us
to:
A beautiful, autumn-cum-winter day. CAMERA FINDS Dwight,
serenading Vivian on the clarinet as she sips soup from a thermos.
After unearthing the grave of Charlotte Charles
in search of a pocket watch and finding neither
girl nor watch, Dwight resolved to use his
masculine wiles to determine whether Vivian
knew of her niece’s final, final resting place.
He finishes his song, Vivian offers her applause.
The clarinet is a lovely instrument. I always
wanted to be a flautist, but unusually tight
tendons in my pinkie finger made hitting D-
sharp impossible.
Dwight takes her hand and examines her pinkie. Then keeps
holding it, the sly devil.
They look just fine to me. Perfect for holding.
I’m not the kind of woman who slips notes into
random men’s coat pockets. But something
about you...
(wary)
And what might that have been?
The charm you force to cover the brutish shell
around your damaged heart. I like layers.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED:
For a moment, and only a moment, Dwight felt his
cold heart warm ever so much.
Funny. Lily was under the impression you were
only looking to recover some personal
property, then disappear like a puddle of
gasoline in the sunshine.
I was saddened to hear Charles’s watch was
buried with your dear late niece. But what a
fine gesture that was. I imagine the service
was magnificent.
It was a big funeral.
So others, beside yourself, were able to see
poor Charlotte at peace with the watch, before
her dear soul was committed to ground?
Mary Suddbury leaned in and peeled back
Charlotte’s eyelids. Said there was a
vigorous black market for stolen corneas, but
I thought it was in poor taste.
(a sigh, then)
Charlotte meant the world to me. In a way, I
feel responsible for her death...
She withdraws her hand, feeling a sudden (unexpected) swell of
emotion.
You know fine and well you can’t shoulder the
burden of blaming yourself for her death.
Oh, but I do... I do. I encouraged Charlotte
to take the pleasure cruise that ended so
unpleasantly. I was tired of being a shut-in,
but I couldn’t bring myself to leave so I
decided to leave vicariously and pushed
Charlotte out the door. Poor Charlotte.
Now, look. You’ve gone and set those pretty
peepers a-weeping. Have a little more soup,
honey.
Vivian reaches into her purse, removing a LAMINATED COPY of
CHUCK’S OBITUARY.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED: (2)
I’ve carried this with me since the funeral...
as a reminder to stop living vicariously and
start living-living.
She hands the obit to Dwight.
VIVIAN (CONT’D)
You’ve probably seen her face before. She was
all over the news after she died.
Dwight fights to keep his mouth from dropping... he recognizes
her, all right.
I’ve definitely seen her face before.
OFF him...
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 22.
OMIT
Emerson, Ned and Chuck sit in a booth with Daniel Hill.
Do you know if Gustav ever donated to an
organization called the Bellmen?
The Bellmen?
Every house that’s been robbed got a call from
a Bellmen telemarketer named Tam Fong.
(impassioned, booming)
So this Tam Fong killed Gustav? Where is
he? I’m gonna find that malfeas-ass and
slam him down...
Inside voice.
(whispering)
...and I’m not talking about the gavel of
justice...
Outside voice.
...I’m talking about Southern-style, back-
alley score settling doled out by a tribunal
of me and a couple of homeless I’m gonna pay
to pummel--
Conversational patio voice?
Especially when it comes to talk of fisticuffs
and threats of bodily harm.
I have a thousand affirmative defenses for
when I “snap” and smite Gustav’s killer.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 23.
CONTINUED:
Whoa now. Before you go dolin’ out blind
justice, the smoking gun doesn’t always point
to the bad guy.
So Tam Fong isn’t the guilty party?
Yes. No. Maybe. All we know is, maybe he
had a hand in marking the mark.
The good news is, we have a reason to believe
that Gustav completed a second will.
That’s great news! Hopefully that tarnished
trophy wife of his is excluded. But I’m his
lawyer. If there were a second will, I would
have drafted it, drawn it up and drawn a tidy
20% commission for my troubles. So how would
you know differently?
Let’s just say our procedures would be
inadmissible in court. Either way, the will
appears to have been taken in the robbery.
You people really mix the good with the bad.
The world would be a better place if everybody
dabbed a little Calamine on welts of bad news.
Gustav Hofer deserved better than the wife he
had, and the wife he had doesn’t deserve the
money he earned. You find that will, I’ll
double your fee.
(sympathetically) (avariciously)
We’ll find that will. We’ll find that will.
Daniel stands and exits as Olive approaches.
We know Tam’s calling the houses to be robbed
even if he’s not robbing them. Maybe we
should add our names onto his do-call list.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 24.
CONTINUED: (2)
No burglar worth his burgles gonna take the
bait when they see your tiny-ass apartments.
We could use my aunts’ house?
Ooh! A sting! Can I sting? I wanna sting!
That ain’t a bad idea.
That’s a very bad idea.
It’s a good idea. Made doubly-good because
while you’re figuring out who brought the
lights down on Gustav Hofer, I’ll be shining a
light on the true identity of Dwight. I have
an old cigar box filled with my dad’s letters
hidden in my bedroom. If Dad did know Dwight,
maybe I can find something about him inside.
The Pie-Maker considered the wooden box in her
old room a better alternative to the wooden box
that contained her father, so a sting was set.
Tam, at his desk, looks up to find Olive standing in the
doorway, dressed as a multi-millionaire and leading Pigby on a
diamond-studded leash. She hangs up his phone.
Mr. Fong, I am so sorry to interrupt. I’m
Tessa Carville, wife of Clarence Carville, who
I’m sure you’re aware owns Carville Steel. I
believe someone here called me yesterday?
(jumps to his feet)
Mrs. Carville, of course! Please, take a seat.
I won’t be staying long, just long enough to
explain how much I hate phone solicitations.
Almost as much as I hate beggars and
panhandlers. I believe I have the right to a
net worth greater than most developing
countries without being hounded by sponging
ne’er-do-wells and sanctimonious bleeding
hearts like yourself.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 25.
CONTINUED:
So unless you stop calling, I’ll use a tiny
fraction of my immense wealth to buy this
building, knock it down and turn it into a
glue factory so big the whole city will be
smelling horse.
Tam’s expression has, understandably, darkened.
If you please leave me your number, I’ll see to
it that nobody ever calls you again. Psych.
Did you say, “Psych”?
No.
Olive hands him her phone number.
Good, because I’m getting on a hovercraft for
Saint-Tropez early this evening, and I expect
it dealt with before I return tomorrow.
OFF Olive, gotcha--

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - CHUCK’S BEDROOM

lines.text: Filled with CHEESE. The once-empty bedroom has big wheels,
small wheels, moldy, holey, shelves, refrigerators, etc. The
window slides open and Chuck crawls into the room. A second
later, and Ned follows.
Aw. They’ve turned my old room into a cheese-
locker! Can you smell the flowery overtones
of the Stilton wafting through the air?
It’s nice that they filled this room with
something you all loved so much.
It’s amazing how a familiar smell can wrap you
in its arms and coddle away any ugly memories
between now and the last time you smelled it.
Thank you. For letting me come along.
I’m glad you came.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 26.
CONTINUED:
And don’t worry about getting caught. I’ll
hear anybody coming before they even get to
the staircase.
Chuck goes to the corner and pulls the loose sideboard away,
revealing a TIN CAN with a STRING coming out the bottom.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
The other end is hooked to the big Victrola in
the living room. I used it when I was a
teenager to eavesdrop on my aunts.
That’s very crafty.
Chuck smiles. Ned ducks back out the window. Alone in her room,
Chuck goes to the opposite corner, pulls a loose floorboard away
and produces an ornate old cigar box from within.
Alone in a room that was once hers, Chuck
felt, for a moment, like a little girl again.
Thinking of the mementos in the box, among
them the birthday present she was never able
to give her father, Chuck thanked her 8-year-
old self for the kind act of leaving them here
for her now-self to rediscover.
Thank you, 8-year-old self.
She pries open the box, smiling at the eclectic mix of old U.N.
memorabilia and a handmade, leather wallet.
OFF Chuck...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM

lines.text: Olive, Vivian and Lily eat cheese and sip tea in the dimly-lit
room. Behind them, Emerson and Ned are casually SHUTTING OFF
LIGHTS, BLOWING OUT CANDLES.
You must be out of you damn minds -- there’s
no way in Tinkerbell’s bitsy buttcheeks you’re
going to be rolling out the welcome mat on my
front porch to a bunch of thieves.
We know it’s an imposition--
“An imposition”? An imposition is ordering
clams at a kosher deli.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 27.
CONTINUED:
Robbers nowadays are multi-hyphenate hoodlums.
They don’t just rob. They strip you naked,
lather you in lard, slide you into the walls and
leave you there. Then they rob you. And burn
your house down.
When you put it that way--
Why don’t I just grab a shovel and start
digging my shallow grave now?
I find a dash of danger titillating.
Lily rolls her eye.
You’ve certainly made that clear.
Vivian pulls Lily aside. Olive follows.
I assume that’s a passive-aggressive insult
directed at my daring sashay into romance. So
I choose to ignore it.
May as well, you’ve ignored every other
warning sign on the road to abject heartbreak.
I find that interjecting at precisely the
right moment often defuses a conflict.
Wouldn’t you agree?
Lily Charles, you’re jealous. It simply slays
you that a man so tender and viscerally
masculine as Dwight chose me over you.
Missed it by that much.
I’m not jealous. I’m worried about you. I love
you and I don’t want to see your fetish for
raffish men hurt you the way it has in the past.
Ned approaches.
On the topic of Dwight--
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 28.
CONTINUED: (2)
Keep out of this.
Lily was just about to tell me that I let
myself become seduced. By a bad boy
named Charles Charles. But Charles was a
good man. He was the one seduced... by
some cheap harlot in pasties and a merkin
that had the misfortune of dying in
childbirth.
Emerson closes the BAY WINDOW BLINDS behind Lily.
Is my patch on the wrong eye or is it suddenly
very dark in here?
Is it dark? I didn’t even notice. They say
extreme photosensitivity can be a sign of
rabies. Or a hangover. Or a delicate optic
nerve condition--
Or a bunch of part-time P.I.s trying to
hoodwink a hoodlum by pretending my house is
vacant. Wait... are we being robbed tonight?
Ooooh, I just got a shiver.
Lily grabs her SHOTGUN.
Good idea. Arm yourself. That way, if the
robber comes, you can--
CLICK. Lily cocks the gun. Points it at Emerson. Aghast, the
Mod Squad realizes she’s pissed at them.
Put that pea shooter down. We’re just asking
you to aid in the apprehension of a robber.
Slash-killer. Sorry. Not helpful.
Oh, what the hell.
Lily BLOWS out the last candle. In the darkness we HEAR her re-
cock her gun.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 29.
CONTINUED: (3)
LILY (CONT’D)
Got my dander up enough that I wouldn’t mind
shooting someone right about now.
(to Vivian)
Why don’t you give Loverboy a call?
The CAMERA TRACKS into the blackness of the Victrola’s mouth...
While the bickering downstairs continued...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - CHUCK’S BEDROOM - CONTINUOUS

lines.text: ...AND PULLS OUT again from inside the TIN CAN Chuck’s just
pulled away from her ear.
...Chuck decided she had heard all the fighting
she cared to, and turned her attention instead
to her father’s dusty belongings.
Chuck pulls a PHOTO from the box--
INSERT - A PHOTO OF YOUNGER DWIGHT, sitting on a camel’s back
and wearing a United Nations uniform. He is flanked by NED’S
FATHER and CHUCK’S FATHER (photo drawn from IMAGE in Ep. 206).
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Seeing Dwight engaged in male bonding with her
father and the Pie-Maker’s father, she wanted
to shout downstairs that Dwight was, in fact,
who he said he was, and that perhaps there was
nothing to worry about after all...
On Chuck, gazing at the photo.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...but as she was hiding from Lily and Vivian,
she could not shout downstairs. Not about a
photo...
BACK to include the OPEN WINDOW, and the SHADOWY FIGURE gazing
down at Chuck--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...or anything else.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 30.

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - CHUCK’S BEDROOM

lines.text: DIRECT PICK-UP where we left off. Chuck leaps to her feet to
find herself face-to-face with Rob Wright, head of the Bellmen.
Fear not -- OW!
Chuck hurls her wooden box, hitting him square in the head. Rob
wobbles back against the wall, holding his head.
ROB (CONT’D)
Fear not, madam. I mean you no harm.
Spectacular throw, by the way.
To be fair, I should warn you that I have a
gun in my pocket.
To be fair, I don’t really believe you.
To be even more fair, all I have to do is
scream and a whole cadre of big, strong men
and sweet middle-aged ladies with shotguns
will come running.
Fair enough. And yet, you haven’t. Perhaps
because you understand society has a moral
obligation to protect the least fortunate in
its ranks... and where society fails--
You pick up the slack. Which sounds noble
until you go and kill somebody. At which
point it becomes plain evil.
I’m no killer, merely a soldier of fortune.
Other peoples’ fortunes for the underprivileged.
Gustav Hofer says otherwise. Or would, if he
could speak, which he can’t since he’s dead.
You and Tam Fong killed him two nights ago.
After you robbed him.
First of all, Tam Fong is but another
unwitting victim of my robberies. I swipe his
phone list to choose my targets.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 31.
CONTINUED:
And Gustav?
I robbed him, it’s true. Not because he was
stingy and uncharitable, but because he asked
me to.
He asked you to rob him?
He was writing a new will and needed to know
whether to name his wife as the beneficiary.
I know how this must sound, but the facts
were these:
Huh?
These were the facts:
Gustav exits the store, passes a bell-ringing, Bellmen-outfit-
wearing Rob Wright, who is collecting donations. Gustav doesn’t
make eye contact, patting for his keys as he makes for his
ROLLS ROYCE.
ROB (V.O.)
I met Gustav in the midst of a crisis of
faith. His decision to rewrite his will had
made him question whether he had any true
friendships, or merely a gaggle that clung to
him for his wealth.
Gustav stops patting when he spies the keys in the ignition. He
puts his head down on the roof of the car. Rob ambles over.
ROB (V.O.)
It didn’t take much to push him over the edge
into a full-fledged late-life crisis. And
that’s when we met.
ROB - Has been watching, removes the HANGER that hoists his
donation bucket. Sets off.
AT THE CAR - Rob jimmies the lock of the Rolls, opens the car
door. Gustav goes for his wallet, but Rob stops him.
ROB (V.O.)
He wanted to make a contribution, but I
wouldn’t let him. He said:
(as Gustav speaks)
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 32.
CONTINUED:
ROB (V.O.) (CONT'D)
“Where I come from, people get paid for their
services.” But I said:
(as Rob speaks)
“Charity is an impulse, not a return for a
friendly act.”
Gustav looks at the collection pot, then at Rob.
ROB (V.O.)
So we talked. He told me his problems and I
offered a solution.

scenes.heading: INT. GUSTAV’S MANSION - TROPHY ROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: INSERT - A CASE OF JEWELRY is emptied into a canvas bag. Next,
a box of SILVERWARE...
ROB (V.O.)
I agreed to rob him. He would liquidate his
bank accounts, put the money in his safe and
appear to be an innocent victim. If his wife
stayed faithfully by his side, his concerns
could be laid to rest. Regardless, I’d
return half his fortune and keep the other
half for charity.
Rob inspects the trophies, then smiles as he spots a latch
attached to the lion’s paw. He gives the lion a twist and the
safe door CLICKS open.
ROB (V.O.)
I was just unloading the contents of his
secret safe when...
The LIGHT flicks on and Gustav’s wife, Elise, stands in the
doorway. She quickly snatches an ANTIQUE HUNTING MUSKET from
the wall, points it at Rob, finger clearly on the trigger.
ROB (V.O.)
...Gustav’s wife intervened with a musket...
As Rob dashes nimbly out a side door with his canvas bag.
ROB (V.O.)
...and I had to get out.

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - CHUCK’S BEDROOM

lines.text: Resume, as before.
I read in the paper the next day about what
happened to Gustav.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 33.
CONTINUED:
Even if you didn’t kill him... you’re still
a criminal.
My duty is to the downtrodden, the meek, those
unable to reach their own bootstraps let alone
pull them. I take only what people can afford
to lose, and that certainly doesn’t include
their lives. Do you like puppies?
Yes.
The Papen County Animal Shelter is going to be
shut down tomorrow unless I get them the money
to pay their mortgage. And with nowhere to
house the animals, the dogcatchers are calling
it “The Big Sleep.”
And you can save them.
As long as the help outweighs the hurt, an act
of charity always makes sense.
NED (PRE-LAP)
You let him go?

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - NIGHT

lines.text: Ned stares at her, shocked. Emerson’s beside him, not shocked
at all.
What if he’s a cold-blooded killer?
It was an act of charity and... there were
puppies involved. Besides, my Grueneberg
ganglia hadn’t activated.
That sounds personal.
Maybe this is one of those feminine
conversations you want to have with your
lady friends.
There’s a little bundle of nerves at the tip of
your nose that can detect aggressive pheromones.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 34.
CONTINUED:
As in, you can sniff out danger.
And what I smelled was a swashbuckling do-
gooder in the wrong place at the wrong time.
Smells like puppy crap to me.
You shouldn’t have let him go. It was a
mistake.
Chuck notices Ned clenching and unclenching his fists.
You’re really mad at me, aren’t you?
I’m out of counter space, so I’m stress
baking in my head.
I feel like you’re stress baking me.
I’m channeling fear into anger.
Anger leads to hate.
Hate leads to stress baking the people you love.
Which is bad, but better than stress
releasing. Like you did for the Bellman.
Maybe we should consider Rob Wright was
telling the truth. Maybe his musket-toting
wife dropped the chandelier on him.
(to Emerson)
You did say the bellman-slash-porter was
hiding something. He may have an alibi, but
maybe he knows who killed Gustav.
CUT TO:
Chuck and Ned sit with Emerson as he peers through binoculars at
Gustav’s mansion. Through the binocs, he spies James-Andrew
readying for bed.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 35.
CONTINUED:
Stakeouts are only fun when there’s binoculars
for everybody.
Stakeouts are only fun when you got a good
football game to listen to and the stake
you’re outing is next to a hot dog vendor.
They seem like a good time to have weighty
conversations--
No, they don’t.
If Dwight figures out I’m not dead, it might
be the best thing that ever happened to me.
You talking a lot like a dead girl who wants
to go back in the ground.
What is the worst that could happen?
Pie-Maker becomes a sideshow in the Circus of
Fun and I earn my wages peddling tickets.
This is a cavalier conversation about a deep,
dark touchy subject for me.
How deep, dark and touchy is it?
Ever since I was little, I’d have this dream
where somebody learned what I could do. It
starts out with lots of ice cream and
balloons, and ends up in a small white room
where little bits are cut out of me until
there’s nothing left to cut.
That’s awful. Dwight represents the embodiment
of those anxieties and you still don’t want to
wake up my dad to find out about him. You put
my emotional well-being above your fears.
That’s so courageous... and romantic.
Thank you.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 36.
CONTINUED: (2)
Well, looky, looky.
Emerson’s peering through the binoculars again. James-Andrew
has been joined by Elise in the boudoir for a heavy-petting
session.
Isn’t that Gustav’s widow? And the bellboy?
Petting?
James-Andrew and Elise kiss passionately and laugh.
Hello, motive, nice to see you again.
All that remained for Emerson Cod was to
confront the bellman and widow about their
illicit affair. And across town...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK AND OLIVE’S APARTMENT - NIGHT

lines.text: CAMERA FLOATS TO FIND CHUCK’S WALNUT VANITY, where her FATHER’S
POSSESSIONS have been lovingly arranged.
...all that remained of Charles Charles was a
daughter’s loving box of memories.
DRIFT PAST a blue beret, medals, aviator sunglasses, then the
picture of Dwight, Ned’s dad and Charles...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The man who had set so much in motion was
long gone...
CAMERA STOPS on her father’s POCKET WATCH...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...but the man who intended to bring it all to
a crashing end...
A HAND reaches in and takes the watch.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...was not.

scenes.heading: INT. LIBERTY APARTMENTS - ELEVATOR - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Through the old-fashioned cage elevator, we find DWIGHT,
studying the watch with a wicked smile. As the elevator drops
OUT OF FRAME:
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 37.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - NIGHT

lines.text: Olive is putting the chairs on the table, closing up for the
night. The door JINGLES open--
We’re closeuhhh...
She trails off when she turns to find Dwight standing menacingly
in the doorway. She pulls it together.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Excuse me. I have a rare type of narcolepsy
where only my mouth falls asleep. I meant to
say, “We’re closed.”
So you’re here, all by your lonesome.
He’s dropped the charm for menace, and Olive suddenly realizes
that she is indeed alone.
I’m not here all by my lonesome. Manuel, the
big cholo janitor, is in the back. I think he
was in one of those super-dangerous El
Salvadoran gangs that murders older white men as
a warning to the police not to mess with them.
(calling off)
Isn’t that right, Manuel? He’s probably
cleaning the toilet.
I’d like to leave a message for your friends.
Sure thing. I’ll just go grab you a pad...
Olive moves to the counter and bends over to grab a pen and paper.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
I hope you don’t need an envelope or--
She stands, surprised to find Dwight gone. He’s left something
on the table he was standing beside.
While Olive Snook was unable to provide the
pen and paper she sought...
Olive picks up the paper he left, and her eyes widen as she
realizes -- it’s Vivian’s laminated clipping of Chuck’s
obituary.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 38.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...she’d received the mysterious Dwight’s
message loud and clear.
OFF her, freaked out...
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 39.
CLOSE ON: Vivian’s laminated clipping of Chuck’s obituary.
1 hour, 23 minutes and 42 seconds ago, Olive
Snook made 2 alarming discoveries: First, that
the dark stranger, Dwight Dixon, had discovered
Chuck, aka, Charlotte Charles’s, true identity.
We PULL OUT to see the clipping is flecked with bits of pie
crumbs. Dollops of ice cream plop on the clipping.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Second, that in time of duress, the Pie-
Maker's penchant for stress baking was matched
only by the petite waitress’s predilection for
stress binging. Though this nervous habit
greatly lightened her cleanup load...
PULL OUT FARTHER to see Olive, uncomfortably full, surrounded by
EMPTY PIE TINS. One SWOOP sends all the tins into the trash.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...it did little to lighten the load in her
heart as she anxiously awaited the Pie-Maker’s
return.

scenes.heading: INT. GUSTAV’S MANSION - TROPHY ROOM - NIGHT

lines.text: Emerson, Ned and Chuck confront a sheepish James-Andrew and Elise.
It’s a classic tale. You bumped off Gustav so
you could keep bumpin’ uglies with the bellman
while inheriting a fortune.
I told you. Alibi. Key party.
(to Elise)
But your alibi didn’t check out. You never
showed up at the charity ball. Why’d you do
it, Elise?
I didn’t do anything. Except James-Andrew.
Who do you think got his key?
Ooooooh. I was still really wrong about what
I thought that was.
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 40.
CONTINUED:
(back on the case)
You two backin’ each others’ alibis means
bubkes. You were canoodlin’ and cahootin’ and
you cahooted to kill.
We cahooted to keep quiet about our affair.
Adulteresses, like, totally get the shaft in
estate law.
(then)
Whatever. That weasly, little lawyer probably
ratted me out ages ago.
Mr. Hill?
Who else? He caught me with James-Andrew and
totally flipped his grits. Lectured us about
how Gustav was some great dude who deserved
respect and loyalty. But I’m great, too, and
I deserved nookie -- not just nights of sponge-
bathing some senior --
(jealous)
You never sponge-bathe me...
(showcasing her fingernails)
I don’t sponge-bath anyone anymore, baby.
Since I grew these puppies out, my manicure
means I’m a mani-can’t for manual labor.
You were a mani-can when it came to pointin’ a
gun at the robber, Rob Wright, and almost
pulling the trigger.
As if! I never saw the robber. Even if I did--
Elise strides toward the MUSKET hanging on the wall and grabs
it, pointing it at the Mod Squad. They back away, hands up.
Why’s everyone pointin’ guns at me?
There’s no way I could pull the trigger on a
gun. I’m too blinged out!
PUSHING DAISIES #207 "Robbing Hood" 09/04/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 41.
